subject: Re: Recap & Mutual Action Plan — ACME POC (call 2026-02-20)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cope@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Hayes <samantha.hayes@acme.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & Mutual Action Plan — ACME POC (call 2026-02-20)

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Wanted to capture the quick recap and a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) so we have aligned owners, milestones, and dates. Please flag anything we missed or want to move.

Key pain points you shared:
- High per-token cost and unpredictable latency on current vendor during peak batch runs (customer-facing recommendations).
- Lack of tooling for route-based fallbacks and on-prem options for regulated data flows.
- Need for stronger observability (per-route token cost and latency breakdowns) to hit their SLOs.

Goals for the pilot (POC):
1) Validate response latency under representative load (95th percentile target < 500ms).
2) Demonstrate 30% reduction in per-token cost with caching/batching/quantization configs.
3) Confirm integration path for private deployment of customer-sensitive pipelines (VPC/on-prem proof).

Decision process and timeline (what we heard):
- Technical approval: Platform team (Samantha + Tom) will validate POC results.
- Security & legal review: Internal security + legal at Acme (Samantha to loop in contacts).
- Exec sponsor sign-off: VP Product (target decision after POC & security greenlight).
- Target decision date: week of 2026-03-29 (approx 5 weeks).

Proposed Mutual Action Plan (high level):
- Feb 22: Kickoff call + access details exchanged (owners: Marissa (Redwood) / Samantha (Acme))
- Feb 25: Provisioning + baseline perf run (owners: Jordan / Acme infra)
- Mar 5: Mid-POC check-in + initial cost report (owners: Ben / Samantha)
- Mar 20: Final POC results, security & compliance review shipped (owners: Marissa / Acme security)
- Mar 29: Decision review with execs (Acme VP Product)

Open items / asks from Acme for POC success:
- Provide sample traffic profile and expected peak RPS for the customer-facing recommendation workflows.
- Provide legal contact for SOC2/contract redlines (Samantha noted internal legal).
- Confirm desired dataset retention policy for the POC (default: 30 days unless otherwise requested).

Attachments: I attached a short Mutual Action Plan PDF and our security overview for the POC.

Next steps (from Redwood):
- I’ll send calendar invites for kickoff and provisioning windows (by EOD Monday).
- Jordan will reach out with the provisioning checklist and temporary keys.
- Ben will prepare an initial cost estimate based on the traffic profile once received.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.coal@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf, redwood-security-overview.pdf

From: Samantha Hayes <samantha.hayes@acme.com>

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the items below and adding a couple clarifications: 

- Decision timeline: aiming for final review week of 3/29 but our legal review might push that by a week if there are redlines; I’ll try to keep it within the month.
- Legal contact: forwarding to legal@acme.com (we’ll expect a one-week turnaround on SOC2 doc review).
- Traffic profile: I’ll send a CSV with hourly RPS by endpoint by EOD Monday — includes peak estimations and typical payload sizes.

On stakeholders: I will be the technical lead for the POC and Tom will be the infrastructure owner for provisioning. I’ll also invite our security engineer (Leah Park) to the kickoff once she’s looped in by legal.

We’re OK with the proposed MAP dates; kickoff on Feb 22 works for us. Do you have a preferred window? Morning PST is best for our infra team.

Thanks — Samantha
Samantha Hayes

Samantha / team — quick follow from the infra side:

- For provisioning: we’ll need a short-lived service account + IP allowlist for the POC. Jordan will send a checklist.
- Cost estimate: once we get the traffic CSV, I’ll run a baseline and a tuned config estimate (caching + batching) and share numbers by Mar 1.
- Security: can Acme confirm whether the POC requires encryption-at-rest keys managed by you (bring-your-own-key) or if Redwood KMS is acceptable for the trial? This affects our onboarding checklist.

Also tagging legal redlines: if legal@acme.com wants to push early redlines, we can accept an NDA addendum or standard SOW — happy to surface a light timeline to keep the decision on track.

Thanks — Ben

Thanks team — quick logistics note and updated MAP with owners/dates below. I’ll send calendar invites for Feb 22 kickoff (09:30 PT) — Jordan will include the provisioning checklist in that invite.

Updated Mutual Action Plan (v1.1):
- Feb 22, 09:30 PT: Kickoff call (Owners: Marissa / Samantha) — Agenda: access, scope, success metrics
- Feb 25: Provisioning complete + baseline perf run (Owners: Jordan / Tom) — deliverable: baseline perf report
- Mar 1: Initial cost estimate (Owners: Ben) — deliverable: tuned cost model (PDF)
- Mar 12: Mid-POC check-in (Owners: Marissa / Samantha) — deliverable: interim results & any blockers
- Mar 20: Final POC results + security package (Owners: Marissa / Acme security) — deliverable: final report + SOC2 evidence summary
- Mar 29: Executive review & decision (Owners: Acme VP Product / Marissa) — deliverable: decision and next steps (SOW or pilot expansion)

Decision criteria (what will make this a success):
- Performance: 95th pct latency < 500ms on representative traffic
- Economics: >= 30% unit cost reduction or clear path to reach it with Redwood configs
- Security: SOC2 evidence + acceptable data retention and KMS approach

I’ve attached the MAP and our security overview for your legal/security feeds. If legal wants a specific contract template, please send it to contracts@redwood.ai and we’ll have our legal team prioritize.

Looking forward to the kickoff — see you Monday.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
